title: `Range::_calc_value` clamps value to unexpected value when `allow_greater` is false.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot 4.4.1, 4.0  (and likely all in between given age of code)

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot Mono v4.4.1

### Issue description


According to the documentation: `allow_greater` flag on `Range` :

> If true, [value](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_range.html#class-range-property-value) may be greater > than [max_value](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_range.html#class-range-property-max-value).

However when  setting the `page` of a Range where `allow_greater` is `false` the following code triggers as `set_page` triggers a re-calculation of `value` via [Range::_calc_value](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/gui/range.cpp#L141)

```c
if (!shared->allow_greater && p_val > shared->max - shared->page) {
    p_val = shared->max - shared->page;
}
```

This actually tries to clamp the value not to max, but max minus the page size.  This isn't too tragic normally, but if you span into the negative it starts to cause unexpected behavior. 

e.g.
Value = 0
Min = -128
Max = 64
Page = 192

Setting the page size to 192 causes the value to be changed to -128, since it's checking to see if the value (0) is greater than 64 - 192 (-128). Which it is and then is erroneously "clamping" to that number.

A decent workaround is to set `allow_greater` to true before setting the page size, then restoring the to false after.


### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
	var range = Range.new();
	range.set_min(-128);
	range.set_max(64);
	range.set_page(192);
	if range.value != 0:
		print("Value change to %f" % range.value)
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[range-bug-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21689222/range-bug-repro.zip)
